notes: budget.go:123 `fencesContent` is a hand-maintained tool-name allowlist decoupled from the only real criterion (`contentFence` at format.go:207, used at format.go:179 and 421). Nothing fails if a third formatter starts wrapping content in a fence — that tool silently keeps the old miscount-and-short-cut behaviour. A test asserting the two lists agree would close this; no current defect.

budget.go:131-133 the comment says "Every other formatter writes the indexed content as prose", but `formatRepositoryMap` (format.go:379) does wrap pretty-printed JSON in a ```json fence. Harmless in fact (MarshalIndent never emits a line starting with `### ` or `- `, and that path is byte-for-byte main's), but the comment overstates the rule.

clampResponse's `strings.LastIndex(text, "\n### Notes\n")` (budget.go:41) is still fence-unaware, as the implementer flagged. Verified it is unchanged from main and not worsened: on a read-file answer whose content holds a literal `### Notes` line the split still lands inside the fence, leaving an orphan closing fence after the notice. Pre-existing, out of this scope.

The `#### ` code-search rule is still keyed on the `## Code Search\n` prefix (codeSearchHits, budget.go:197) rather than the tool name, so the diff leaves two different discriminators in one file. Checked: no other formatter produces that prefix, so no live defect — but the next change here should unify them.

Release note wording: scope the claim to read-file and get-symbol-context. The prose formatters (search-semantic, find-runbook, search-code, export-context, query-docs) deliberately keep main's behaviour, and the upstream cause — `parse` at internal/indexer/indexer.go:1110 splitting on headings without fence state, which produces the unbalanced chunks — is untouched. Fixing that would change the reindex fingerprint.

Verified reversibility: code-only, no schema or migration, no external state. The audited `result_count` for read-file moves from a content-derived number to 0 and get-symbol-context stays at 4; only the admin console reads the column and no doc pins its semantics (grep over docs/ and web/ for `result_count` is empty).
